title: Momentum docket — weekly growth & experiments
body:
Quick framing: this is my rolling note for personal targets, small experiments, and weekly course corrections. Treat as the single source for what I actually ship and measure — not the lofty roadmap.

Topline targets (6-week window):
- Reduce "time-to-first-sample" for new SDK users from ~4.2m -> <2.5m (measured as median time from signup -> first successful run of examples).
- Increase sample-template adoption (starter templates used in repo forks) by 25%.
- Close 3 small docs gaps that repeatedly cause support tickets (streaming JSON examples, auth edge-cases, env var troubleshooting).
- Run 2 small UX experiments that might reduce onboarding drop-off (A/B template ordering, simplified error messaging).

This week — quick pulse (Mon -> Fri):
- Wins: landed streamlined sample that drops the boilerplate; UX copy for auth errors merged (PR #1198).
- Slow/messy: getting signal for template adoption is noisy — forks aren't a reliable proxy. Need better instrumentation.
- Blockers: analytics event team bandwidth; need one event to track "first run success".

Quant metrics (latest snapshot):
- New dev signups (last 7 days): 142
- Median time-to-first-sample: 3m 58s (down from 4m 12s two weeks ago)
- Template repo forks: +8% week-over-week (currently 312 forks)
- Docs support threads referencing "auth issue" (rolling 30d): 19
- PR throughput (my area): 4 small merges this sprint, 2 pending reviews

Hypotheses / experiments (short):
1) If we put a "Run this in <1 click>" banner on the templates page, more users will try the live example -> increases first-run success.
   - Signal: spike in live-run events + lower median time-to-first-sample.
   - Plan: banner + one-button runner (feature flag) for 2 weeks.
2) Clearer error messages for token/auth will reduce support threads by ~30%.
   - Signal: fewer support threads + better CSAT on auth category.
   - Plan: iterate on 3 messages, ship copy + link to troubleshooting doc.

Open asks / dependencies:
- Analytics: need event "sample_run.complete" with success boolean and elapsed_seconds. Pitched to analytics; follow up with Priya.
- Infra: small container for live-run environment needs 2GB ephemeral quota increase for scale test (ticket with infra: INF-314).
- CS: can we get a short list of 5 anonymized repro steps from recent auth tickets? (ask Arjun)

Concrete next actions (next 7 days):
- Monday: add instrumentation ticket + pair with Maya to spec event schema. (est 1.5h)
- Tuesday: prototype banner with one-click runner, run local usability with 3 new hires. (est 4h)
- Wednesday: ship auth copy changes + link to troubleshooting doc. (est 2h)
- Thursday: sync with analytics and infra; unblock event and quota changes. (est 1h)
- Friday: short retrospective + update this file with outcomes and numbers. (est 30m)

Retrospective notes (end of week template):
- What moved the needle? (quant + qualitative)
- What wasted time? -> flag and try to eliminate next week.
- What to change in experiments? -> tighten signal definitions + shorter cycles.

1:1 agenda items for my manager (next):
- Quick update on onboarding metrics + ask for priority on analytics event.
- Proposal: dedicate 0.5 engineer-day/week for two sprints to finish starter templates instrumentation (shows ROI).
- Feedback request on copy clarity and whether shipping incremental fixes is favored vs larger rewrite.

Notes to self / heuristics:
- Prefer small, measurable experiments over large rewrites. 2-week cycles are ideal for learning.
- If instrumentation is missing, lean on qualitative usability tests (3 users) rather than waiting for perfect events.
- Keep a running note of exact search terms users use when they open support tickets — they are gold for copy improvements.

Scattered quick items (scratch):
- Add a short checklist to the template README: 1) set API key, 2) run example, 3) check logs.
- Draft email to CS to ask for top-5 repro steps.
- Save link to internal demo recording: (link in linked_artifacts).

-- end of current rolling entry --
(Will append outcomes after Friday run-through and mark which experiments to continue/kill.)
